metadata.title: Stock Market Today: Tech Stocks Lead Futures Sharply Lower; Oil Prices Surge on Middle East Escalations

content.text:
Stock futures pointed sharply lower Thursday, another busy earnings day, with tech stocks leading declines. Meanwhile, crude prices jumped on reports that the U.S. and Israel plan to renew attacks on Iran.
Nasdaq 100, S&P 500, and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were down 1.6%, 0.9%, and 0.6%, respectively.
Yesterday, the major U.S. indexes closed higher, led by big gains for tech stocks on another busy day of earnings reports. The benchmark S&P 500 rose 0.7% for its third straight day of gains.
Chip and other AI-tied stocks sold off early Thursday. Roundhill's Memory ETF (DRAM) dropped 4% before the bell, pulled lower by components Micron Technology (MU), Sandisk (SNDK), Seagate Technology (STX), and Western Digital (WDC), which is slated to report results after markets close today. The broader iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) also declined roughly 4%, dragged down by the likes of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Intel (INTC), and Nvidia (NVDA).
The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS), which tracks the Magnificent Seven mega-cap tech stocks, was about 2% lower premarket, with a nearly 5% drop in Tesla (TSLA) shares following the EV maker's earnings report weighing. Meta Platforms (META), which also issued quarterly results yesterday afternoon, slipped 1%.
Shares of SpaceX (SPCX) were down 2.5% before the bell. The space, AI, and social media company led the Nasdaq 100 with an 8% advance Wednesday after it posted its first quarterly profit and CEO Elon Musk said that the board and Tesla's formed committees to discuss a merger.
Crypto-tied stocks, including Strategy (MSTR), Mara Holdings (MARA), Coinbase Global (COIN), and Robinhood Markets (HOOD), fell sharply as the price of bitcoin declined to roughly $82,000 from overnight highs around $84,800.
Big-name companies reporting results before markets open today include Procter & Gamble (PG), Lockheed Martin (LMT), Honeywell International (HON), Union Pacific (UNP), Norfolk Southern (NSC), Spotify Technology (SPOT), and Comcast (CMCSA).
Oil prices jumped on reports that the U.S. and Israel were planning on resuming military strikes against Iran, as well as increased attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia. U.S. benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude futures were up 2.1% to $99.15 a barrel in recent trading. Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, were 2.6% higher at $111.60.
The 10-year Treasury yield fell to around 5.07%, down more than five basis points from Wednesday's close. The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the value of the greenback against a basket of foreign currencies, slipped 0.1% to 101.64. Gold futures fell 1.1% to $4,105 an ounce.
